blocks.text: Prompt chaining breaks a complex task into a sequence of smaller, focused prompts, where the output of one step becomes the input to the next, a general workflow decomposition pattern rather than a technique tied specifically to reasoning difficulty.

This topic covers why breaking one large prompt into a chain of smaller ones helps, how this differs from least-to-most prompting covered in an earlier module, the real debugging advantage chaining provides, and the added cost of running multiple sequential calls.
1. What Prompt Chaining Means

blocks.alt: Building on prompt iteration, prompt chaining introduces sequential prompt calls

blocks.text: Prompt chaining structures a task as a sequence of separate prompt calls, each one focused on a single, well defined sub-task, with the output of each step feeding directly into the next, rather than attempting the entire task in one large, multi concern prompt.
2. One Big Prompt vs a Chain of Focused Prompts

blocks.alt: One big, complex prompt is compared against a chain of smaller, focused prompts

blocks.text: A single prompt asked to extract key facts from a document and then write a polished summary from those facts is handling two genuinely distinct concerns at once, splitting this into two chained prompts, one focused purely on extraction, one focused purely on summarization, lets each step do its one job well.
3. A Simple Two-Step Chain Example

blocks.alt: Step 1 extracts key facts, step 2 summarizes from those facts

blocks.text: The first step in this example takes the raw document and extracts a clean list of key facts, the second step takes only that extracted list, not the original document, and produces a polished summary from it, each step has a narrow, clear responsibility.
4. Prompt Chaining vs Least-to-Most Prompting

blocks.alt: Least-to-most decomposes by difficulty, prompt chaining decomposes as a general workflow

blocks.text: Least-to-most prompting, covered in an earlier module, decomposes a problem into subproblems ordered specifically by increasing difficulty, all building toward the same underlying reasoning task, prompt chaining is a broader pattern, decomposing any multi step workflow into stages, which may have nothing to do with escalating difficulty, extraction then summarization is a workflow split, not a difficulty progression.

blocks.text: 5. Passing Data Between Chain Steps Reliably

blocks.alt: Step 1 output gets parsed cleanly and passed as step 2 input

blocks.text: For a chain to work reliably, the output of each step needs to be in a form the next step can actually consume cleanly, this connects directly to structured outputs, covered in an earlier module, a step producing well formed JSON or a clearly delimited list is much easier to feed into the next step than unstructured free text.
6. The Debugging Advantage, Isolating Which Step Failed

blocks.alt: When something goes wrong, the failure can be isolated to step 1 or step 2

blocks.text: When a chained pipeline produces a wrong final result, inspecting the intermediate output at each step reveals exactly which stage actually introduced the problem, a single large prompt handling everything at once offers no equivalent way to isolate where a failure originated.

blocks.title: This mirrors a familiar software engineering advantage
blocks.content: Breaking a large function into smaller, single purpose functions makes bugs easier to isolate in traditional software, prompt chaining provides the same debugging benefit for a multi step AI workflow.

blocks.text: 7. The Cost, More Calls and More Latency

Every additional step in a chain means an additional model call, adding to both latency and cost, this is the same fundamental tradeoff seen with self-consistency and tree of thoughts, covered in an earlier module, more calls in exchange for a benefit, in this case modularity and debuggability rather than accuracy.
8. When to Chain vs When One Prompt Is Enough

blocks.alt: A simple, single concern task needs only one well crafted prompt, a complex, multi concern task genuinely benefits from chaining

blocks.text: A task with one clear, single concern rarely benefits from chaining, one well crafted prompt handles it fine, a task genuinely combining several distinct concerns, extraction, transformation, formatting, each with its own failure modes, is where chaining earns its added cost and complexity.
9. Chaining as a Prompt Optimization Tool

Within this module theme of optimization, chaining is a structural tool, sometimes breaking a poorly performing monolithic prompt into a chain of smaller, more focused steps improves overall accuracy and reliability even accounting for the added latency, a genuine optimization tradeoff worth testing against the metric-driven iteration process covered in the previous topic.
Worked Example

A developer builds a single prompt that reads a legal contract and both extracts key clauses and rewrites them in plain language simultaneously, results are inconsistent, sometimes missing a clause, sometimes producing plain language that subtly misrepresents the original legal meaning.

Splitting this into a two step chain, first extracting clauses precisely with an instruction focused purely on completeness, then rewriting only the extracted clauses in plain language with a separate instruction focused purely on clarity, produces more consistent, complete results, and when an error does occur, it becomes immediately clear which of the two steps actually introduced it.
Common Mistakes

items: Chaining a genuinely simple, single concern task where one well crafted prompt would have sufficed
Passing unstructured, hard to parse output between chain steps instead of a clearly structured format
Not accounting for the added latency and cost multiple sequential calls introduce
Confusing prompt chaining, a general workflow decomposition, with least-to-most prompting, which is specifically about difficulty progression

blocks.text: Practice

Take a task you have handled with one large, multi concern prompt before, identify two genuinely distinct concerns within it, split it into a two step chain, and compare the reliability and debuggability of the chained version against the original single prompt.
Key Takeaway

Prompt chaining breaks a complex, multi concern task into a sequence of smaller, focused prompts, each handling one clear responsibility, offering a genuine debugging advantage by isolating exactly which step causes a failure, at the real cost of additional latency and calls, making it worth reserving for tasks that genuinely combine distinct concerns rather than a simple, single purpose request.
